entries.sense_en: a fine, smooth cloth once made of wool or silk, used for cloaks
entries.sense_ko: 외투 등에 쓰던 고운 모직·견직 천

synonyms.nuance: Dense, smooth wool cloth; the fabric of a gentleman's fine coat, more upmarket than camlet.
Plain everyday word for the material; camlet names one specific old, fine weave.

entries.sense_en: showing the ill effects of too much drinking; grossly given to drink

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for being drunk or given to drink; lacks crapulous's sense of sick, sordid aftermath.
Morally loose in general (drink, sex, money); wider than crapulous, which is about excess drink.
Suffering the morning after; temporary and informal, while crapulous is a lasting, literary condition.

entries.sense_en: unsteady and shaky, as if about to fall

synonyms.nuance: Informal; anything that shakes from side to side, not only weak people.
Trembling from weakness, fear or age; focuses on shaking rather than nearly falling.
Walking unsteadily and violently, from a blow or drink; stronger and more sudden than tottering.

entries.sense_en: if it was really necessary; in an emergency

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; simply says it will be done when required, without hinting at hardship.
synonyms.example: I can stay late if need be.

synonyms.nuance: The usual American form of the same idiom; "upon a pinch" is the older British wording.
synonyms.example: In a pinch, we can walk.

synonyms.nuance: British informal; means barely managing, only just possible.
synonyms.example: We can seat ten at a push.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서는 in a pinch / at a pinch를 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: an old word for a stroke: sudden collapse from bleeding in the brain

synonyms.nuance: The everyday modern medical term for the same event.
synonyms.example: He had a stroke last year.

synonyms.nuance: Broader: any sudden attack, including epilepsy, not only a brain bleed.
Informal, vague sudden attack; also used for anger (a fit of rage).
synonyms.example: He fell down in a fit.

entries.sense_en: a person who owns land or property, here a large landowner

synonyms.nuance: Plain, everyday word for anyone who owns anything.
Specifically owns land; proprietor is broader and more formal, often a business owner.
Owns property that others rent, or runs a pub; not simply an estate owner.

entries.sense_en: confused and slow-minded from drinking

synonyms.nuance: Only mildly drunk and cheerful; fuddled is duller and more mentally muddled.
synonyms.example: a little tipsy after two glasses

synonyms.nuance: Slang for very drunk; blunt and modern, not about a confused mind.
Confused, from drink or anything else (a hard problem); wider than fuddled.

entries.sense_en: to talk in a hypocritical, pious way about religion or morals

synonyms.nuance: Speak earnestly about morals, often sincerely; cant is always insincere.
Lecture others about right and wrong, usually tiresomely; not necessarily false.
Talk like a preacher in a long, self-righteous way; mocking tone.

entries.tip_ko: can't(~할 수 없다)와 전혀 다른 단어지만, 미국 발음은 둘 다 /kænt/로 같다.

entries.sense_en: a quick sharp tap or flick with a finger

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a quick snap of finger or wrist.
Light touch or knock, not a snapping motion.
A sharper, harder knock that makes a sound.

entries.sense_en: the look and expression of a person's face

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, everyday word for the physical face.
Only the feeling shown on the face, not the whole face.
Literary, formal synonym of countenance; somewhat grand or grim.

entries.sense_en: a habitual drunkard

synonyms.nuance: Neutral-negative word for someone often drunk.
British informal and friendlier; can also mean a pub.
Clinical word for someone addicted to drink; not a moral insult like sot.

entries.sense_en: deprived of courage or self-control by strong emotion

synonyms.nuance: Upset by a shock; milder and much more common today.
Made afraid or anxious; close in meaning, but modern and not about manliness.
Overpowered by emotion, sometimes fainting or weeping; stresses strength of the feeling.

entries.tip_ko: 보통은 '무인의'(unmanned aircraft)라는 뜻이지만 여기서는 '기가 꺾인'이라는 옛 뜻.

entries.sense_en: poor and shabby, with worn-out clothes

synonyms.nuance: Nearly identical: shabby and run-down from poverty, but suggests lost status.
Short of money; says nothing about appearance.
Informal: has no money right now, possibly only temporarily.

entries.sense_en: for the sake of old times and old friendship (Scots)
entries.sense_ko: 옛정을 생각하여, 그리운 옛 시절을 위해

synonyms.nuance: Plain English equivalent; less sentimental and no Scots flavor.
synonyms.example: Have one more drink for old times' sake.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, explanatory phrase; lacks the traditional song feel.
synonyms.example: He came in memory of old days.

entries.tip_ko: 새해 송년 노래 '올드 랭 사인'의 그 표현이다.

entries.sense_en: wooden panelling on the lower part of a wall

synonyms.nuance: General word for wood panels on walls, high or low.
The lower part of a wall, whatever its material; technical.
Only the narrow board along the bottom edge of a wall.

entries.sense_en: great trouble or distress; a trying experience

synonyms.nuance: One severe, testing experience that you get through.
Ongoing lack of comfort or money.
A lasting cause of suffering, such as an illness.

entries.sense_en: grabbed and held tightly, in fear or urgency

synonyms.nuance: Seize suddenly; does not imply holding on.
Hold firmly, as a steady, strong hold.
Take forcibly and suddenly; more formal and often violent.

entries.sense_en: choked, as if squeezed by the throat

synonyms.nuance: Suggests a cry cut short as if the throat were squeezed.
Blocked breath, from smoke, emotion or food.
Held back on purpose, muffled.

entries.sense_en: went over the main points again

synonyms.nuance: Short, informal form of the same word.
Give the short version, not necessarily a repeat of what was said.
Look back over something to check it, not just repeat it.

entries.sense_en: getting a secret out of someone slowly and cleverly

synonyms.nuance: Gentle persuasion, friendly.
synonyms.example: I coaxed the truth out of her.

synonyms.nuance: Bring a person into telling something, with no trickery implied.
Formal: get information by effort or force.

entries.tip_ko: worm out of ...은 '~에서 슬쩍 빠져나가다'라는 뜻으로도 쓰인다.

entries.sense_en: a junior teacher who shows students how to do practical work

synonyms.nuance: General helper; demonstrator is a specific teaching role.
Teaches students individually or in small groups, rather than showing procedures.
The everyday modern meaning of demonstrator (a marcher); not this sense.

entries.sense_en: a person who enjoys good food, drink and company

synonyms.nuance: Cares about fine food in particular.
Formal; refined taste in food and wine.
Chases fun of any kind; less refined.

entries.sense_en: passed down as a duty to a particular person

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase: become someone's job.
Someone deliberately hands the task over; devolve is more automatic.
synonyms.example: The task was delegated to Ann.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral movement from one person to another.
synonyms.example: The title passed to his son.

entries.sense_en: people who come where they are not wanted

synonyms.nuance: Enters a place without permission; can be dangerous.
Legal term: enters someone's land unlawfully.
Simply not part of the group; no wrongdoing implied.

entries.sense_en: morally low and mean, tied to greed or dirty dealing

synonyms.nuance: Dirty and wretched, about physical conditions.
Shabby and slightly disreputable, milder than sordid.
Poor or unfair, not necessarily immoral.

entries.sense_en: a small amount of something good

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a small amount of anything.
A barely noticeable amount.
Usually used in negatives: not a shred of evidence.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 a modicum of + 명사 형태로 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: beyond criticism; so correct that no fault can be found

synonyms.nuance: Perfect, faultless, often of manners or style.
Cannot be blamed; formal, about conduct.
Has no defect at all, for objects and performances.

entries.sense_en: a fair exchange: something given for something received

synonyms.nuance: Paying back like for like, often harm for harm.
Giving up one thing to gain another.
synonyms.example: a trade-off between price and quality

synonyms.nuance: Neutral swap of things.

entries.sense_en: looking guilty, shameful and low

synonyms.nuance: Looks untrustworthy; eyes that avoid you.
Mildly embarrassed; much gentler than hangdog.
Secretive and sneaking.

entries.sense_en: rough, violent, lawless men

synonyms.nuance: Violent criminal hired or used for force; current word.
Rowdy, destructive young person, often British.
Dishonest but often charming; not necessarily violent.

entries.sense_en: people who rob graves and take dead bodies

synonyms.nuance: Literal: steals from graves; not a monster.
Undead creature that drinks blood; different horror figure.
Spirit of a dead person; ghouls deal with the body.

entries.sense_en: moved by dragging the feet, awkwardly and uneasily

synonyms.nuance: Walk slowly and clumsily, from tiredness or age.
Move sideways or slyly toward something.
Move quietly from guilt or shame.

entries.sense_en: to be a sign of something

synonyms.nuance: General, common word for pointing to a fact.
Formal: mean or stand for.
Warns of something bad to come.

entries.sense_en: living recklessly for pleasure, wasting health and money

synonyms.nuance: Morally loose; stress on immorality more than waste.
Corrupted by sex and drink; stronger.
Careless of danger; no moral judgment.

entries.sense_en: willing to do wrong to get what he wants

synonyms.nuance: Has no firm moral rules.
Shows no pity in pursuing goals; not always dishonest.
Simply lies or cheats; plainer and weaker.

entries.sense_en: bold, daring, self-confident style

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for willingness to take risks.
Informal; can mean rude cheek ("what a nerve").
synonyms.example: He had the nerve to ask.

synonyms.nuance: British; disrespectful boldness.

entries.sense_en: to violate a sacred place; here, by digging up its graves

synonyms.nuance: Treat sacred things with contempt; often in words.
Break a rule or sacred place by force; wider.
Damage property for fun; not about holiness.

entries.sense_en: suspicious, suggesting something wrong

synonyms.nuance: General: arousing doubt.
Suggests dishonest people or deals.
British informal: risky or of doubtful honesty.

entries.sense_en: the less you talk about a problem, the sooner it is forgotten

synonyms.nuance: Do not stir up a problem that is quiet now.
A plain request to stop talking about it.
synonyms.example: Let's say no more about it.

synonyms.nuance: Stay silent; informal.

entries.sense_en: fussy, timid people who are easily scared

synonyms.nuance: American informal: someone who worries over nothing.
Childish word for a coward.
Someone who makes a fuss over small things.

entries.tip_ko: old wives' tale(미신)과 같은 계열의 표현. 여기서는 성차별적 경멸어.

entries.sense_en: began to like someone suddenly

synonyms.nuance: Slightly more steady, less whimsical.
synonyms.example: She took a liking to him.

synonyms.nuance: Grow gradually fonder; slower.
Deeply and romantically attracted.

entries.sense_en: kept giving him drinks, one after another

synonyms.nuance: Urge someone to accept something.
synonyms.example: He pressed more food on us.

synonyms.nuance: Give a lot at once, often gifts or praise.
Give someone a heavy amount at once; lacks ply's sense of offering again and again.

entries.tip_ko: ply A with B: A에게 B를 계속 권하다/퍼붓다.

entries.sense_en: thought over slowly, brooding on something

synonyms.nuance: Think unhappily and at length.
Formal for chewing cud; deep, calm thinking.
Think carefully about a choice; neutral.

entries.sense_en: a state of being temporarily set aside; not working

synonyms.nuance: Stopped for a time, often officially.
Uncertain waiting state.
Inactive but able to wake.

entries.sense_en: stiffness of a body after death

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; also for sore muscles.
Unwillingness or inability to bend or change.
Medical term for the stiffening of a corpse.

entries.sense_en: the decision was made and could not be undone
entries.sense_ko: 주사위는 던져졌다, 돌이킬 수 없게 되었다

synonyms.nuance: Plain, describes the situation.
synonyms.example: Now there is no turning back.

synonyms.nuance: Make a bold, irreversible decision.
The moment past which you cannot go back.
synonyms.example: We reached the point of no return.

entries.sense_en: make final and certain

synonyms.nuance: Make a deal final, as with a signature.
End an argument or matter.
Make safe or win; wider.

entries.sense_en: money, thought of as dishonestly gained

synonyms.nuance: Neutral gain from business.
Stolen goods or money.
Everyday word for ready money; no bad tone.

entries.sense_en: a hangman's rope; here, risking being hanged

synonyms.nuance: Loop of rope used to hang someone.
The structure for hanging.
Neutral; only context makes it a hanging rope.

entries.tip_ko: 보통은 말 머리에 씌워 끄는 굴레(밧줄)를 뜻한다. put one's neck in a halter는 '교수형을 무릅쓰다'.

entries.sense_en: the person who decides someone's fate

synonyms.nuance: Officially decides a case.
Rules on a game.
Helps two sides agree, without deciding.

entries.sense_en: a partner in a crime

synonyms.nuance: Legal term: helps a crime without being the main criminal.
Informal, sometimes joking.
Plans the crime together in secret.

entries.sense_en: to be proud of oneself and show it

synonyms.nuance: Feel proud of a quality, often justified.
Talk about one's achievements openly.
Show off in the way one walks or acts.

entries.sense_en: cloth wrapped around a dead body

synonyms.nuance: The usual word for a sheet on a corpse.
Old term for a shroud.
Plain modern phrase.

entries.sense_en: a digging tool like a pickaxe with a broad blade

synonyms.nuance: Pointed head for breaking hard ground.
Lighter garden tool for weeding.
Flat blade for lifting soil.

entries.sense_en: the Last Judgment, the end of the world

synonyms.nuance: Religious name for God's final judgment.
General, non-religious.
synonyms.example: until the end of the world

synonyms.nuance: Biblical, formal.

entries.sense_en: small drinks of strong liquor

synonyms.nuance: A small taste of any drink.
A big gulp from a bottle.
British: small measure of spirits.

entries.sense_en: boasted

synonyms.nuance: Common word for bragging.
Informal; more annoying.
Show off by manner.

entries.sense_en: feeling one's way in the dark

synonyms.nuance: Handle clumsily.
Neutral; move by touch.
Trip while moving.

entries.sense_en: dug up out of the ground

synonyms.nuance: Formal synonym; dig from a grave.
Dig up anything, also facts.
Everyday phrasal verb.

entries.sense_en: long, wailing howls

synonyms.nuance: General loud cry of dogs or wind.
Sad, high cry.
Most general.

entries.sense_en: ghostly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word.
Strange, frightening.
Ghost-like, unreal.

entries.sense_en: acted first, preventing him from speaking

synonyms.nuance: Act first to take away someone's chance.
See it coming and act ahead.
Stop; without the timing idea.
